title: Caloric restriction modulates genome-wide somatic mutation in mice
title_zh: 热量限制调节小鼠全基因组体细胞突变
abstract: Somatic mutations accumulate throughout life in every cell, and this process constitutes one of the hallmarks of aging-genomic instability. Caloric restriction (CR) has been shown to extend lifespan across diverse species. Using high-fidelity duplex DNA sequencing of bulk liver, bulk kidney, hepatocytes, and cerebellar neurons, we found that CR in mice reduces genome-wide somatic mutation burdens across multiple tissues and cell types. CR reduced both substitution and insertion/deletion burdens, with the magnitude of these effects varying across sample types. CR also decreased the activity of the enigmatic single-base substitution (SBS) mutational process SBS5 that gives rise to most mutations in mammals. Surprisingly, the mutation burden reduction from CR was greatest in transcriptionally inactive regions. This work illuminates links between diet, aging, and genomic integrity and establishes genomic integrity as a modifiable axis of aging.
abstract_zh: 体细胞突变在整个生命周期中在每个细胞中累积，这一过程构成了衰老基因组不稳定性的标志之一。热量限制（CR）已被证明能延长多种物种的寿命。通过对小鼠全肝、全肾、肝细胞和小脑神经元进行高保真双链 DNA 测序，我们发现 CR 能降低多种组织和细胞类型的全基因组体细胞突变负荷。CR 降低了替换突变和插入/缺失突变的负荷，其效应大小在不同样本类型中有所差异。CR 还降低了神秘的单碱基替换（SBS）突变过程 SBS5 的活性，SBS5 是哺乳动物中大多数突变的来源。令人惊讶的是，CR 对突变负荷的降低在转录不活跃区域最为显著。这项工作阐明了饮食、衰老与基因组完整性之间的联系，并确立了基因组完整性作为可调节的衰老轴。
